mechanism: Bin RSI_20 into 10 deciles (0-10…91-100); on train, accumulate signed future close direction (look_ahead=20 M1 bars) per bin into a transition/count matrix; greedy rule maps positive bins to buy and negative to sell (later probability form P(up|bin)). Learns symbol-specific RSI regime structure instead of fixed 30/70.
data_needed: ~300k M1 OHLC; RSI(20); binary Target from close vs close.shift(-20); train/test split.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: NZDJPY M1 primary; RSI rolling-std also compared on XPDUSD vs NZDJPY/NZDUSD
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS an explainable RSI-state → directional-tendency regime sensor fitted per symbol rather than universal overbought/oversold thresholds.
quote: On the training set, we grouped the RSI readings into 10 bins, from 0-10, 11-20, linearly until 91-100. We recorded how price behaved in the future, as it passed through each group on the RSI.

mechanism: Compare rolling standard deviation of RSI across markets (precious-metal XPDUSD vs FX NZDJPY/NZDUSD) to show that the same RSI reading implies different extremity under different RSI volatility; argues entry thresholds must be market-specific.

mechanism: After fitting the Markov greedy rule, measure per-bin validation accuracy; discard train-dominant 41-50/61-70 artifacts; select OOS-best bullish zone 11-20 (~75%) and bearish zone 71-80 for NZDJPY entries (EA opens buy/sell only in those bands; optional exit on opposing RSI zone or MA cross).
data_needed: Hold-out RSI and Target labels; per-bin accuracy table; optional EMA for MA_Close mode.
why_new_for_mis: Separates train mass from OOS reliability—MIS can treat per-state predictive accuracy as a meta-sensor for which oscillator zones are currently informative.
quote: On the validation set of the data, we obtained the highest accuracy when we bought in 11-20 range, and sold in the 71-80 range. We had accuracy levels of 51.4% and 75.8% from the respective zones.

mechanism: Split train in half; refit RSI-bin P(up) matrix on first half; feed Markov Predictions (and optionally OHLC+RSI+Predictions) into MLPClassifier(20,10) with RobustScaler and TimeSeriesSplit; compare Transition Matrix vs Deep Markov vs OHLC-only vs All—Markov and Deep Markov beat raw OHLC (~0.519 vs ~0.497 test) but deep stack did not beat the simple matrix.
data_needed: Markov Predictions column; scaled OHLC/volume/spread/RSI; Target; TSCV with gap=look_ahead.
why_new_for_mis: Shows stacking a neural net on a probabilistic transition feature as a sequence/regime sensor—and that the Markov feature alone can dominate raw quotes for MIS baselines.

mechanism: Build nominal bar features: bar_type bullish/bearish; body_type from |C-O|/|H-L| into bins ≥0.75, ≥0.5<0.75, ≥0.25<0.5, <0.25; bar_pattern higherHigh / lowerLow / flat from two consecutive same-direction bars with both high and low shifted. Target = next-day log-return.
data_needed: Daily OHLC; sequential bar comparisons; look_ahead=1 log close return.

mechanism: CNomOrd maps each nominal class to mean target percentile rank (outlier-robust vs raw mean encoding); score() runs Monte Carlo target shuffles and returns P(observed max−min class-mean gap arises by chance). fitTransform can collapse many nominals to one ordinal via ArgMax class-id. Used to show only bar_type associates with BTCUSD next-day returns (p≈0.0005) while body/pattern do not.
data_needed: Feature matrix with categorical column indices; aligned target vector; permutation reps (e.g. 10000).
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a supervised categorical→ordinal sensing transform plus a permutation association gate so weak nominal sensors can be rejected before entering the stack.
quote: The score() method is used to assess the statistical significance of the implied relationship between an ordinal variable and a target. A Monte Carlo permutation test is employed to repeatedly shuffle the target variable data and recalculate the observed relationship.
